Turkish Land Registry Appointment for Foreign Buyers: What to Expect

The title-transfer appointment is the visible end of a property purchase, but most problems should be solved before that day. Foreign buyers benefit from knowing which documents, interpreter arrangements, payments and title details must already be in order.

Published: 8 September 2026 · Ozan Ferhat Şen, Attorney at Law

For a foreign buyer, the Turkish land registry appointment can feel like the decisive moment of the purchase. In reality, it should be the final execution step of a transaction that has already been legally checked.

1. The property details should be settled before the appointment

The buyer should already know the registered owner, parcel or independent-unit details and whether the title carries mortgages, attachments, annotations or third-party rights. The appointment is not the ideal moment to discover that the property record differs from the sales presentation.

2. Identity documents must be consistent

Passport information, translations and other identity records should match. Differences in spelling or transliteration can create avoidable complications, especially where documents have been prepared in several countries or languages.

3. Interpreter requirements should be arranged in advance

Where the buyer cannot conduct the official procedure in Turkish, an interpreter may be required. The practical requirement should be confirmed in advance so that the transfer is not delayed by a missing interpreter or unsuitable document.

4. Payment timing deserves its own plan

Buyer and seller should understand when the purchase price will be paid and how that timing relates to the transfer. A property transaction should not rely on vague assumptions about whether money is transferred before, during or after registration.

5. A power of attorney changes who attends, not what must be checked

If a representative attends for the buyer, the power of attorney must contain the authority required for the specific transfer. The title, contract and payment structure still require the same legal attention as a transaction completed personally.

6. International buyers may search for the appointment in their own language

A German-speaking buyer may search Grundbuchamt Türkei Termin or Tapu Termin Türkei; a Russian-speaking buyer may search запись в земельный кадастр Турции or оформление тапу в Турции; an Arabic-speaking buyer may search موعد الطابو في تركيا. The wording varies, but the practical concern is the same: what must be ready before the official title transfer takes place?

7. Fees, taxes and transaction costs should not be a surprise

Before the appointment, the parties should know which official fees and other costs apply and which party is expected to bear them under the transaction documents.

8. What should already be checked?

  • Registered owner and property identifiers
  • Mortgages, attachments and annotations
  • Buyer’s eligibility to acquire the property
  • Required identity documents and translations
  • Interpreter arrangements where applicable
  • Power of attorney if a representative will attend
  • Payment sequence
  • Official fees and transaction costs
  • Any contract conditions that must be satisfied before transfer

The appointment should be boring

That is usually a good sign. The safest land-registry appointment is one where the difficult questions have already been answered and the parties are simply completing a transaction whose legal structure is understood.

Official sources

  • General Directorate of Land Registry and Cadastre: Procedures Guide for Foreigners
  • TKGM: YourKeyTürkiye

Preparation before the appointment reduces last-minute risk

Title records, powers of attorney, translations and payment sequencing can be reviewed before the land-registry appointment so that the transfer day is an execution step rather than a troubleshooting session.
